visual_invariants: Motor, inverter, reduction and differential live as one removable rear cassette, not a lab axial brick train on a skid.
Default packaging uses a transverse rotor axis into a spur reduction and final drive without a bevel stage when space allows.
Pulse inverter shares the cassette volume — rigidly on the motor/gearbox face or inside the same structural envelope (above/ahead), not a remote brick on a separate base.
Modern rear units are single-speed (or minimal-ratio) reduction plus differential; casing length is set by gear mesh and shaft exits, not shift drums.
HV DC interface faces the battery with a short stiff bus; AC phase paths to the stator are the shortest possible inside the case.
Cooling jackets, manifolds and dual fluid loops (motor vs inverter) define bosses and outer envelope language — not a clay-smooth motor sculpture.
Driveshaft exits at axle height fix lateral width and case split planes; the unit must clear suspension rockers.
Public exterior language is a sealed structural case (ribbed Al or CF) with fastener grids, coolant/oil ports and HV connectors — windings and PCB farms are cutaway-only.
Mass and CoG push a low compact cassette behind the battery; inverter is forced low when packaging allows.
Service is whole-cassette removal: mechanical mounts, two thermal loops, HV and LV/control interfaces — not field-open motor service.
